purpose: reader-facing explanation of the supported image-to-story-to-podcast workflow

required_facts.fact: The published project turns a photo of an everyday object into a story, illustration, narration, website post, and Spotify podcast episode.
required_facts.evidence: Source line 3: the AI writes, illustrates, and narrates from a photo and publishes to the website and Spotify via RSS.

required_facts.fact: The input is selected from a local folder or an S3 input bucket.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 90-93: the script picks the first available image from images_input or the S3 input location.

required_facts.fact: GPT-4o receives the image and a constrained prompt for a Russian horror story with a title and URL slug.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 95-113: image input is sent to GPT-4o and the prompt specifies story, title, and slug requirements.

required_facts.fact: The story prompt requests eight to twelve paragraphs and excludes several title and plot patterns.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 102-106: paragraph count and exclusions for title words, whispers, rustling, and returning objects.

required_facts.fact: GPT-5 is used after generation to clean up Russian grammar and phrasing.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 115-127: the raw GPT-4o story is passed through GPT-5 for editing.

required_facts.fact: The illustration stage uses the first two paragraphs, GPT-4o-mini, and DALL-E 3.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 129-161: the first paragraphs are converted into a scene prompt and sent to DALL-E 3.

required_facts.fact: DALL-E 3 produces a 1024-by-1024 image that is resized and stored in images/.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 161-163: output size, resizing, and storage are specified.

required_facts.fact: Each story gets a sequential ID used in filenames and URLs, and Jekyll saves the post plus image files.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 168-176: sequential IDs and save_story outputs are described.

required_facts.fact: OpenAI TTS tts-1 with the onyx voice creates an MP3 whose metadata is added to the story.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 194-205: text and slug go to generate_tts, then audio URL, size, duration, and assets are updated.

required_facts.fact: RSS XML and GitHub Actions connect the generated files to podcast apps and automated publication.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 213-221: podcast.xml supplies RSS and GitHub Actions pulls, processes, and publishes images.

author_attribution: Explain Alexey's historical implementation as documented; do not present the project-specific model choices as universal technical advice.
